runs.question: what shape does config.toml [hooks] take
runs.method: type-error reverse engineering — feed wrong types and read the serde error

result.matcher_group: { matcher: string, hooks: [HookHandlerConfig] } — every field optional
result.handler: internally tagged enum; variants command | mcp_tool | prompt | agent
result.command_variant: field `command` REQUIRED, type STRING (not an array)
result.trap: `<Event> = [ { command = [...] } ]` PARSES CLEANLY and yields an empty matcher group with zero hooks — a valid config with zero dispatch and no warning

runs.question: how does a hook become trusted, and is there a non-interactive path (A4/A1)
runs.method: app-server `hooks/list` for key+currentHash, then write [hooks.state."<key>"] into the scratch config.toml; negative control flips one hash byte

result.untrusted_behaviour: silent zero dispatch — no error, no warning, exit 0
result.hook_state_schema: hooks.state is a map key -> struct HookStateToml { enabled: bool, trusted_hash: string }; confirmed by type-error probing
result.negative_control: one wrong hash byte -> trustStatus `modified`, dispatch stays 0
result.cli_override_ineffective: -c hooks.state."<key>"=... has no effect; the key embeds a path so the dotted-path parser splits it. the record must be written into config.toml
result.note: this is the value M1 previously recorded as NOT OBSERVED; it is what let A1 be promoted

runs.question: which hook output format actually stops a turn in Codex, and does the negative control hold (B1/B2)
runs.method: block-probe.js sweep — per-event protected-operation predicate, allow-control first; a blocked verdict requires the hook to have fired AND the protected operation not to have occurred. crashes/timeouts/no-fire are inconclusive, never blocked.

result.negative_control: UserPromptSubmit allow-control reached the protected operation (prompt reached the model)
result.adopted: stdout-json-block — the format receipt-prompt.js already emits, so the gate core needs no second serializer
result.limitation: PreToolUse is UNMEASURED: its allow-control did not reach the protected operation (the model did not use a tool), so no block attempt was run for that event. A missing control makes any blocked observation unattributable.

runs.question: does the real mccp receipt gate actually block a Codex turn when a prerequisite receipt is absent (Metric 2)
runs.method: cli.js gate-demo — scratch CODEX_HOME registers the SHIPPED receipt-prompt-submit.js (not a synthetic payload); scratch repo on a feature branch; MCCP_HARNESS=codex, MCCP_RECEIPT_GATE_MODE=hard. Terminal /mccp:pr is used because a non-terminal gate with a missing-only receipt takes the v1.3.1 informational ALLOW path by design.

result.note: the block payload carried hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName=UserPromptSubmit — the injected event name reached the wire, which a synthetic-payload probe could not have shown

result.directory_copy_alone: NOT discovered — 3 sweeps, control never fired even with a synthesized .codex-plugin/plugin.json
result.official_path: codex plugin marketplace add + codex plugin add — install_ok=true, run-command skill and hooks/hooks.json both present in the installed tree

C2_plugin_root_substitution.reason: the negative control never fired. Four sweeps: config.toml surface (wrong surface — no plugin context), hooks.json after a directory copy (not installed), hooks.json after a synthesized .codex-plugin manifest (still not installed), hooks.json after a REAL install (install_ok=true, yet neither the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} arm nor the ABSOLUTE-PATH control fired). Without a passing control a non-firing observation says nothing about substitution.
